hero.oneLiner: The deck positions SBI as India's largest and most digitally dominant bank — a ~₹76.62 trillion balance sheet with ₹50 trillion gross advances and ₹60 trillion deposits, "Lowest NPA Ratios in 2+ decades", 98.8% of transactions on alternate channels, and a group of listed and unlisted subsidiaries that lead their own segments.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Deck frames the quarter as "SBI delivers Strong & Sustainable Performance" and "Strong Foundations, Building a Future-Ready SBI", anchored on scale: Balance Sheet Size of ₹76.62 trillion as on Jun 26 (₹67.69 trillion Jun 25), Gross Advances ₹50 Trillion and Deposits ₹60 Trillion.
- Claims "Digital Leadership" with No. 1 rank in Debit card spends, ATMs, and value & number of Mobile Banking transactions; stated market shares are 23.65% debit card spends, 31.04% ATMs, 29.40% mobile banking transaction numbers and 24.83% mobile banking transaction value ("as per latest available data").
- Asset quality is presented as a structural strength: "Lowest NPA Ratios in 2+ decades" with Gross NPA 1.47%, Net NPA 0.38% and PCR 74.20% as on Jun 26; Gross NPA ratio has fallen 1.83% → 1.47% over five quarters.
- Loan book positioned as diversified rather than corporate-heavy: RAM Portfolio Share of 66.78% of domestic advances (Per 41.46%, Corporate 33.22%, SME 15.11%, Agri 10.21% as on Jun 26), with ~41% of the corporate book to PSUs / Govt. Depts.
- Group franchise breadth: listed subsidiaries SBI Card (68.58% stake) and SBI Life (55.32%), plus SBI Funds Management, SBI General Insurance, SBI Capital Markets, SBI Payments and SBI SG Global Securities; SBIFML "has been the largest player in the market since Q4FY20" with Q1FY27 quarterly average AUM of ₹12.61 Lakh Crore and 15.12% share versus 13.40% for the second-largest.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Capital position strengthened materially: CRAR 15.67% as on Jun 26 (14.63% Jun 25, 15.40% Mar 26), with CET-1 rising 11.10% → 12.89% against a minimum regulatory CET-1 of 8.80% and minimum total capital ratio of 12.30%.
- Capital efficiency is improving alongside strong loan growth — Credit Risk Weighted Assets on Advances to Gross Advances fell 56.02% (Jun 25) → 53.33% (Jun 26), while RWA to Total Assets moved 53.01% → 52.56%.
- Funding mix has shifted at the margin: SBI SOLO Borrowings rose 42.98% YoY to ₹7,68,854 Cr versus deposit growth of 9.73%; Reserves and Surplus up 20.58% to ₹5,65,908 Cr.
- Subsidiary stake monetisation: the deck footnotes that SBI divested a 6.3007% stake in SBI Funds Management through an IPO during July 2026, taking its holding to 55.56% from 61.86%.
- Domestic CD Ratio at 74.23% (Jun 26) versus 68.88% (Jun 25) and LCR at 126.05% versus 136.67%, indicating balance-sheet liquidity being deployed into credit.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Subsidiary IPO] SBI Funds Management stake reduced to 55.56% after a July 2026 IPO divestment of 6.3007% — an event dated after the 30.06.2026 reporting date.
- [RRB network] 9 SBI-sponsored Regional Rural Banks operate in 9 States across 4,188 branches in 196 districts, with deposits of ₹1,48,806 crores (+8.85% YoY), gross advances of ₹1,25,857 crores (+12.68% YoY), NIM 4.09% and ROE 22.49%.
- [Subsidiary market positions] SBI Life holds private market share of 20.5% in New Business Premium (24.9% individual NBP, 22.2% individual rated NBP, 21.5% total rated NBP) with AUM of ₹5,24,850 Crores and Embedded Value of ₹85,293 Crores; SBI Card is "#2 player in Cards and #2 in Spends" with cards-in-force share of 18.6% (down from 19.1% in Jun 25) but spends share up to 19.5% from 16.6%.
- [Investment banking franchise] SBI Capital Markets' PA&SF Group ranked No.1 in India Borrower Loans (Mandated Lead Arranger) with 36.19% market share (FY26); ECM ranked No.1 in Prime Database by issue amount for Q1FY27; DCM ranked No.7 in Bloomberg's debt private placement league table.
- [Stress pipeline] SMA1 + SMA2 for accounts above ₹5 crores (CRILC) rose to ₹4,174 Cr in Jun 26 from ₹3,350 Cr in Mar 26, and fresh slippages of ₹7,046 Cr in Q1FY27 were the highest of the last five quarters — the one metric moving against the asset-quality narrative.
